name: ACWF World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Held by "Iceman" Greg Smith from the fed's own December 1996 launch; Smith later loses it and publicly blames a UWF wrestler on air, and the belt is still seen in an ACWF duffel bag on a UWF card as late as 3 September 1997, days before the fed's own closure.

name: ACWF Canadian Championship
epitaph: Held by "Cardiac Kid" Joey Valachi, defended on a UWF broadcast 3 January 1997 and challenged for again at the fed's own Beach Wars '97.

name: ACWF World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Three changes across this collection's own holdings: Deadly Intentions (December 1996) lost it to Hellfire and Damnation on the fed's own debut broadcast, which in turn gave way to the New Sensations by mid-1997, who lost it to Lt. Daniel "Lethal" Lawson and Sgt. Mark Sherrick on 23 August 1997 -- the fed's own last recorded title change, won, by the announce team's own admission, on an illegal pinfall.

name: ACWF Tag Team Championship (1996 lineage)
epitaph: A separate, disputed 1996 tag lineage: a two-week reign publicly alleged to have been won by bribery, triggering a formal ACWF investigation and a broadcast exoneration.
notes: The holder and the investigation's own outcome are documented in prose rather than as a dated reigns.json row: the accused holder's name and the investigation's own broadcasts are cited from CWAA's own unheld record, not reproduced under this wing.
